chapters.title: Chapter 3: TDS on Investment Income and Other Payments

lessons.title: TDS on Crypto, Lottery Winnings and Online Gaming

body.text: Crypto, lotteries and gaming sit outside normal slab logic. They carry a flat 30% tax with almost no deductions, and their TDS is designed less to collect your tax than to leave a trail of every trade and every win.

children.text: Aman, 24, a marketing executive in Indore, trades crypto on an Indian exchange. His cousin Pallavi just won a hatchback on a television quiz show. And both of them still have old balances on real-money gaming apps they stopped using when the ban arrived. Each of these situations triggers a very different set of tax rules from salary or FD interest. This lesson covers all three.
Crypto and Other Virtual Digital Assets

markDefs.definition: Digital representations of value generated through cryptographic or similar means that can be transferred or traded electronically, such as cryptocurrencies and non-fungible tokens (NFTs). Often abbreviated VDAs.

children.text: Notice that Aman paid TDS on the Ether sale even though he lost money on it. TDS is charged on what you sell for, not what you make. And although his net profit across both trades is ₹20,000, the tax is calculated on the ₹60,000 gain alone.

body.caption: The Ether loss is simply ignored

body.title: Quick Check: The Ether Loss
body.question: Can Aman reduce his taxable crypto gain by setting off the ₹40,000 loss on Ether against the ₹60,000 gain on Bitcoin?
options: Yes, gains and losses on crypto are netted within the same year
Yes, but only if both trades were on the same exchange
No, a loss on one virtual digital asset cannot be set off against a gain on another, or carried forward
No, but he can set it off against his salary instead
body.explanation: The VDA rules allow only the cost of acquisition as a deduction. A loss on one asset cannot reduce gains on another asset, cannot be set off against salary or any other income, and cannot be carried forward to later years. Each profitable transfer is taxed on its own.

body.title: Try It: Aman's Balance Tax
body.prompt: Aman's tax on his crypto gain is ₹18,720, and ₹3,700 was deducted as TDS on his two sales. How much more must he pay?
body.explanation: ₹18,720 minus ₹3,700 = ₹15,020. The 1% TDS is credited against his total tax, including tax on his salary. Because he owes more than ₹10,000 in total after TDS, he should consider advance tax.

body.text: Trading on a foreign exchange or peer-to-peer does not take you outside these rules. In a peer-to-peer trade the buyer is responsible for deducting TDS, and your gains are taxable at 30% whether or not anyone deducted anything. Indian exchanges report transactions to the department, so crypto activity increasingly shows up in AIS. Report every transfer in the return's VDA schedule.

children.text: Winnings from lotteries, crossword puzzles, card games, game shows, betting and gambling of any kind are taxed at a flat 30% plus cess, under Section 194, Table, Sl. No. 1 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (formerly Section 115BB). No expenses can be deducted, and the flat rate applies even if your other income is below the taxable limit.

cells: A single winning above ₹10,000. Since April 2025 the test is per winning, not the total for the year
The organiser must ensure the tax is paid before releasing a car, gadget or holiday, usually by collecting it from the winner

body.title: Fill in the Blank: The Winnings Threshold
body.textWithBlank: Organisers deduct 30% TDS on a lottery or game show prize only when a single winning exceeds ₹___.
body.explanation: The threshold is ₹10,000 per winning. Someone who wins ₹8,000 three times in a state lottery suffers no TDS, but all ₹24,000 is still taxable at 30% plus cess, which is ₹7,488.

body.title: Scenario: Pallavi Wins a Car
body.scenario: Pallavi, 29, a school teacher in Kochi, wins a hatchback with a market value of ₹8,00,000 on a television quiz show. The producers congratulate her and say they cannot hand over the keys until "the TDS is sorted".
body.prompt: How much tax is involved, who pays it, and does she owe anything more when she files her return?
body.modelAnswer: A prize in kind is still a winning worth its market value, ₹8,00,000. TDS at 30% is ₹2,40,000. Because there is no cash from which to deduct it, the organiser must make sure the tax is paid before releasing the car, so Pallavi will usually have to pay ₹2,40,000 to the producers, who deposit it against her PAN. Her actual tax is 30% plus 4% cess: ₹8,00,000 × 31.2% = ₹2,49,600. After the ₹2,40,000 TDS credit she owes ₹9,600 more when filing. None of this can be reduced by deductions, and it applies even though her teaching salary alone is within the rebate limit. Before accepting a big prize in kind, a winner should be sure they can fund the tax.

body.title: How online gaming winnings have been treated

events.title: Separate online gaming rules
events.description: Net winnings from online games became taxable at a flat 30%, with 30% TDS on net winnings and no threshold, at the time of withdrawal and at year end.

events.title: GST on deposits
events.description: GST at 28% started applying to the full value of deposits on real-money gaming platforms.

events.title: Online Gaming Act enacted
events.description: The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025 received assent, banning online money games of skill and chance alike.

events.title: New Income-tax Act
events.description: The 30% tax on net winnings moved to Section 194, Table, Sl. No. 5 (formerly 115BBJ), and the TDS into Section 393(3) (formerly 194BA).

events.title: Ban takes effect
events.description: The Act and its Rules came into force. E-sports and online social games remain permitted. Constitutional challenges to the ban are pending before the Supreme Court.

markDefs.definition: Broadly, the amount you withdraw from a gaming account, minus the deposits you made and the opening balance at the start of the tax year. TDS at 30% applies to this figure, with no threshold.

body.title: Crypto vs winnings at a glance

columns.label: Crypto and other VDAs
points: 1% TDS on the sale value, above ₹50,000 or ₹10,000 a year
30% tax on gains, with cost of acquisition deductible
Losses are ignored and cannot be carried forward
TDS often locks up cash for active traders

columns.label: Lotteries, game shows and gaming
points: 30% TDS on each winning above ₹10,000, or on all net winnings for online games
30% tax on the gross winning, with no deductions at all
Prizes in kind taxed at market value
TDS is close to the final tax, leaving only the 4% cess to pay

body.title: Crypto, Prizes and Gaming Balances
steps: Download the tax statement from every crypto exchange you use, including the TDS deducted on each sale
Work out gain or loss on each transfer separately, and ignore losses when computing tax
For peer-to-peer purchases above the threshold, check whether you were supposed to deduct 1% as the buyer
Record the market value of any prize in kind and confirm the TDS was deposited against your PAN
Check any old gaming wallet for balances and the platform's TDS statement before withdrawing
Match every entry in your AIS and report VDA transfers and winnings in the correct schedules of your return

body.label: Annual Information Statement (AIS)
body.description: Log in to the e-filing portal to see crypto sales, winnings and the TDS deducted on them, as reported by exchanges and organisers.

cards.definition: TDS at 1% on the sale value of virtual digital assets, above ₹50,000 or ₹10,000 a year. Formerly Section 194S.
30% tax on gains from virtual digital assets, with only cost deductible and no loss set-off. Formerly Section 115BBH.
30% TDS on a single winning above ₹10,000 from lotteries, game shows, puzzles and betting. Formerly Section 194B.
Flat 30% tax on winnings from lotteries, puzzles, card games and gambling, with no deductions. Formerly Section 115BB.
For online games, withdrawals minus deposits and opening balance. Taxed and subject to TDS at 30% with no threshold.
In force from 1 May 2026, banning online real-money games while permitting e-sports and social games.

points: Crypto sales attract 1% TDS on the sale value above ₹50,000 (₹10,000 for some sellers), even on loss-making trades
Crypto gains are taxed at a flat 30% plus cess, only cost is deductible, and losses can never be set off or carried forward
Lottery, game show and betting winnings suffer 30% TDS on any single winning above ₹10,000 and are taxed at a flat 30% plus cess with no deductions
Prizes in kind are taxed at market value, and the winner usually has to pay the TDS before the prize is released
Real-money online games are banned from 1 May 2026, but 30% TDS on net winnings still applies to permitted formats and old balances
Exchanges and organisers report these transactions, so match your AIS and report them in the right schedules of your return
